request.text: We were the Drowned City, the most beautiful place on the coast. Beautiful things are seen. The eye looked at us for one summer, and the sea came up and took the city. The few of us left climbed up here to our hall in the red rock and lifted our stone's shard, and carried it down to the one bay on the coast the eye could not see. The Tide Folk keep it now, under their fire pit. If you came here for it, you came to the wrong shore.
request.voice_description: Native English, a soft, refined Irish lilt. Female, 40-50. Excellent quality. Persona: one of the last survivors of a beautiful city the sea swallowed, writing her people's story in a hall in the red rocks. Emotion: wistful, elegant, sorrowful, dignified, with a cool pride. A clear, graceful, musical voice, unhurried and poised; grief held behind good manners.
